officialExternalParity.interpretation: The existing parity probe is structurally too strict to decide tariff equivalence: it compares the public-map connector tariffs array directly with the external API stored tariff row/array representation. The open-source collector explicitly normalizes both sources to the same consumer output shape, while its public reveData field is only a reduced raw location slice. Therefore 0 raw-object matches is not evidence that the numeric tariffs differ. Connector identity overlap is nevertheless independently proven. EVSE status parity is still unresolved because the current persisted external status keys do not match the identifiers retained in the public reduced slice.
officialExternalParity.nextComparison: Compare semantic tariff components instead of raw JSON objects (currency, energy price, fixed/session/time components and restrictions) for the 32 connector-ID overlaps, and resolve public evse_id/internal-id mapping against the external status records. Reuse persisted samples where possible; avoid a national public sweep.

validationDecision.nextSafeStep: Build a semantic parity comparison on the already proven connector-ID overlap, then run only a small controlled public sample again if additional raw fields are required. Keep the official external collector as canonical until semantic tariff and status parity is demonstrated.
doNot: run a 582-page national public sweep before semantic parity validation
treat the endpoint as official or stable
